question: A $p\text{-}n$ junction diode is connected first in forward bias and then in reverse bias. Compare the barrier potential, depletion region width and current in the two cases. Give reason.

options.A:
Forward bias
The barrier potential and depletion width increase; current becomes small.
Reverse bias
The barrier potential falls and majority carriers give large current.
options.B:
Forward bias
Both currents are equal because bias has no effect on depletion width.
Reverse bias
The diode has no barrier potential.
options.C:
Forward bias
Only minority carriers conduct through a widened depletion layer.
Reverse bias
All majority carriers cross a narrowed depletion layer.
options.D:
Forward bias
The barrier potential decreases, depletion region narrows and large majority-carrier current flows.
Reverse bias
The barrier potential increases, depletion region widens and only a small minority-carrier current flows.
